e-4190.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the first term is $-3$ and the common ratio is $2?$
e-4190.worked_solution:
The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
S_N =\dfrac{a_1(1-r^N)}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, $a_1= -3$ and $r = 2.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{-3(1-{2}^{N})}{1-2} \\  & =\frac{(-3)}{(-1)}(1-{2}^{N}) \\  & =3(1-{2}^{N}).\end{aligned}
$$

e-4191.knowledge_point: Finding the Formula for the Sum of a Geometric Series Given the First Few Terms
e-4191.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of the geometric series $2+8+32+\cdots \: ?$
e-4191.worked_solution:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{8}{2} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
S_N = \dfrac{a_1 (1-r^N) }{1-r}.
$$

In this case, $a_1=2$ and $r=4.$ Substituting these values into the formula for $S_N$ gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{2(1-{4}^{N})}{1-4} \\  & =\frac{2(1-{4}^{N})}{(-3)} \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}(1-{4}^{N}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}({4}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

e-4192.knowledge_point: Finding the Formula for the Sum of a Geometric Series Given an Arbitrary Term and the Common Ratio
e-4192.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $3$rd term is $18$ and the common ratio is $3?$
e-4192.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine $a_1\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 18 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {3}^{(3-1)} \\ 18 & =9{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
S_N = \dfrac{a_1 (1-r^N) }{1-r}	.
$$

In this case, $a_1=2$ and $r=3.$ Substituting our values into the formula for $S_N$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{2(1-{3}^{N})}{1-3} \\  & =-\frac{2}{2}(1-{3}^{N}) \\  & ={3}^{N}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the first term is $3$ and the common ratio is $15?$
content.worked_solution:
The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=3$ and $r=15.$ Therefore, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{3(1-{15}^{N})}{1-15} \\  & =-\frac{3}{14}(1-{15}^{N}) \\  & =\frac{3}{14}({15}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series $4+8+16+\,⋯?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{8}{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=4$ and $r=2.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{4(1-{2}^{N})}{1-2} \\  & =-4(1-{2}^{N}) \\  & =4({2}^{N}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $5$th term is $2\,500$ and the common ratio is $5?$
after.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine ${a}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 2\,500 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {5}^{(5-1)} \\ 2\,500 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {5}^{4} \\ 2\,500 & =625{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=4$ and $r=5.$ Substituting our values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{4(1-{5}^{N})}{1-5} \\  & =\frac{4}{(-4)}(1-{5}^{N}) \\  & =-(1-{5}^{N}) \\  & ={5}^{N}-1\end{aligned}
$$

SN=a1(1−rN)1−r.

after.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $4$th term is $250$ and the common ratio is $5?$
after.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine ${a}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 250 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {5}^{(4-1)} \\ 250 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {5}^{3} \\ 250 & =125{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{250}{125} \\ {a}_{1} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=2$ and $r=5.$ Substituting our values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{2(1-{5}^{N})}{1-5} \\  & =\frac{2}{(-4)}(1-{5}^{N}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(1-{5}^{N}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({5}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}
$$
